protocols.summary: Take an idea, from three words to a short paragraph, through the software delivery cycle (docs/phases.md).

Fix one reported bug in an existing code tree, red first: the bug report is dissected into a checked data document, a test that reproduces the bug is written and observed failing on the unchanged code while the rest of the suite passes, and only then is the fix admissible; the same test and the whole suite must pass on the fixed revision, the bug's story is moved to implemented, and the code tree's gate (build, test, lint, format) passes.
Fix the project context, the vision and the roadmap (docs/phases.md steps 4 to 6).
Deliver one epic of the approved roadmap (docs/phases.md steps 7 to 10).
Turn an idea into a requirements list (docs/phases.md steps 1 to 3).
Decompose the epic's complete ESS specification into AEP stories under the epic.

Release and operate the result of a specification whose stories are delivered: build a release with provenance, run the ESS conformance suite of the current specification revision against it, publish it on a person's approval, and observe it running.
Get the epic's ESS specification to complete (docs/phases.md steps 8 and 9).

Deliver one AEP story of an approved ESS specification: implement it against the current specification revision, verify it with the ESS conformance run against the implementation, have it reviewed, once that run passed, by a principal other than its implementer, and merge it once a person with the merge authority approved that change revision.

limits: **No binary asset.** A user builds from a checkout with `scripts/install.sh --prefix <dir>`; the script is the source of an asset that does not exist yet (`docs/releasing.md`, "The binary").

**The install script builds on the machine it runs on and installs from the checkout it lies in.** It copies only files git tracks and refuses a checkout whose git cannot be asked. Two installs at once into one prefix are not held apart; an install from an archive lacks the links and dot files of a git checkout; a release install after a branch was moved from another work tree is refused until an input of the build changes; a checkout with the reftable format cannot be installed. `scripts/install.sh --help` has each.

**No evaluation run was made on this code.** The records of `experiments/` ran on earlier code; this release claims no measured change over 0.10.0. The fifth Loom evaluation record, `parity-loom-strong-5`, is registered and planned: it has no run yet.

**The rework allowance is not observed in a full run.** The cycle entries that show it, `decider-rework-spent`, `rework-fresh-allowance` and `implement-percause`, stay `pending` (`docs/cycles-suite.md`); no run has told a `rework_limit` of 2 from 3.

**The bindings check follows Loom's decoder for the forms it names.** Five forms (`merge_budget_limit`, `merge_budget_zero`, `merge_budget_unrelated`, `merge_in_action`, `complex_key`) were measured to be refused by Loom when they were measured, at `d8944d49`; no measurement of them at `ed644a4d` is recorded, no other form is claimed refused as Loom refuses it, and the 1 MiB text bound of Loom's reader is not checked (`CHANGELOG.md`).

**The slow lane `task test:loom-in-process` compares a library of `ed644a4d` with the child binary of Loom `70b0e6e0`** (its sha256 is pinned in `runbook/tests/loom_run/slow.rs`); no `b10x-loom` of `ed644a4d` was built for it (`docs/loom-run.md`).

**The recorded cycles run in `docs/cycles-suite.md` is at Loom `d8944d49`.** This preparation did not run `task test:cycles-loom`; the file's last record of the whole suite is 55 cycles, `40 of 40 as expected, 15 pending`.

**Only `runbook run` writes `runner.json`** (`runbook/src/loom_run/run_loop.rs`). A run of the daemon's stub runtime, in which nothing is executed, and a run directory an older `runbook` wrote have none, and the inspector shows them as it showed them before.

**The line of the step in flight is not shown.** Loom pipes a bound program's output into its own process and returns the last bytes when the program ends; the only file that grows while a step runs is under `work/.sdc/llm/`, a dot-directory the inspector never serves (`docs/loom-run-directory.md`).

**`runner.json` and the start lines are what files of the run directory claim.** Under `--confinement local` a bound program can write the run directory, so the inspector's answer is a reading of those files, shown as text, and nothing decides on it.

**A run with no money cap named is not limited in money.** `runbook run` and `sdc-experiment` start a run with no `--cap-micro-usd` and no `--max-llm-calls`; the daemon with `--runtime loom` is the exception, it requires its caps and their ceilings (`docs/loom-run.md`, `docs/daemon-api.md`). A call of unknown cost in a run that names no spend cap books nothing. In a run opened with a model node the printed command of a handoff runs as printed under a named cap too, so several steps spend from one reservation before the cap is looked at again; the story `handoff-under-a-named-cap-runs-one-step-at-a-time` (proposed) is the bound for it.

**A daemon run is read on disk.** Its products are under the daemon's state directory (`runs/<run_id>/` and `workspaces/<run_id>/`, `docs/daemon-api.md`): no tool or route serves them yet, and served by the daemon the Products tab says "the daemon serves no files of a run yet".
**The daemon runs a stub unless asked.** `runbook serve` runs the stub runtime, in which nothing is executed, unless `--runtime loom` is given (`docs/engine.md`).

**The cycles that run `change.review` and the request entries are not observed as `expected` here.** `docs/cycles-suite.md` says that no entry changed from expected to another state is not observed on the host where they were run; it needs one run of the suite at a load where a cycle ends inside Loom's 60 s bound, and that run has not been made.

**No statement about speed, quality or cost goes beyond `experiments/`.** A figure in these notes is a count read from the tree or from a command named above. The times in `CHANGELOG.md` were measured on the build host or the forge and are in no record of `experiments/`.
**The inspector is read-only and has no route to the daemon** (`ui/README.md`).
**`--confinement local` is unconfined** (`docs/loom-run.md`): a bound program can write the whole run directory.
`task check:ess-suite:slow`, the slow lane `task test:cycles-loom`, `task test:install` and `task docs:test` were not run for this release.

A `runbook` started from an installed prefix puts `<prefix>/libexec/runbook` in front of the `PATH` of the programs it starts. Nothing is marked breaking. releases.summary: A minor release of 0.8.0, the same day. The settings file of a run is TOML (it was JSON). The daemon's page starts a run: the daemon lists the runbooks it can start, and its page opens a form (runbook, intake, a confinement level the person picks) that sends `submit-run`. `scripts/check-bindings.sh --exits <root>` checks the exits of a runbook in another repository. The ESS pin is 0.98.0. A source release at tag `0.9.0`; nothing is published to crates.io, there is no binary asset and no interface is stable. `CHANGELOG.md` lists the changes with their sources. Read `docs/releases/0.8.0.md` for the release this one follows.

limits: **No evaluation run was made on this code.** The three runs of record `experiments/parity-loom-strong-4.yaml` ran on the code of 0.6.0 and delivered 0 of 3; all stopped `stuck`. Of the three causes the record showed, the not-called one is fixed by this pin and shown by a no-model test only (`runbook/tests/test_suite/notcalled.rs`); the cause of run 2 (an action dated by the next `evaluated` line) is what `db2726ff` of 0.7.0 changed, also shown by a no-model test only. A rejection still gives the writer no new allowance of runs: `decider-rework-spent` and `rework-fresh-allowance` failed on `RunsSpent` at `db2726ff` and are `pending`; at `c9b4c177` they ended on Loom's 60 s bound (60.6 s and 61.2 s), so the failure is not observed again here (`docs/cycles-suite.md`).

**The cycles that run `change.review` and the request entries are not observed as `expected` here.** `docs/cycles-suite.md` says that the eight entries the layout change may touch were run at a one-minute load of 94 to 156: seven ended `CycleTimedOut` at the bound (`review-reject-once` 62 s, `review-minimal-input`, `review-invalid`, `review-spent`, `implement-request-review-rework`, `coverage-complete` and `implement-request-path-escape`, 60 to 62 s) and `review-invalid-named` ended as expected in 49 s. That no entry changed from expected to another state is not observed on that host; it needs one run of the suite at a load where a cycle ends inside the bound, and that run has not been made.

**`spec-person-wait` and `cite-fault-sent-back` stay `pending`.** The writer loop is gone (the cycles stop `AwaitingPerson`, exit 3), and the person's decision is out of reach of the suite until a step can write a workspace file (no Loom story yet).

**No statement about speed, quality or cost goes beyond `experiments/`.** The release claims no measured change over 0.7.0; a figure in these notes is one that a record of `experiments/` carries, a count read from the tree or a count of a command named above.
**No binary asset.** A user builds from the checkout.

**The inspector is read-only and has no route to the daemon.** It starts no program, takes no decision and sends no command to the daemon (`ui/README.md`). Served by the daemon (`runbook serve --ui`) the Products tab says "the daemon serves no files of a run yet" and lists nothing: the daemon's API has no view of the files, evidence records or output of a run (`docs/daemon-api.md`).

**What the Products tab does not list or serve** (`ui/README.md`, "What a step produced"): a path with a component that starts with a dot (a tool's cache or login), a link that leaves the run, a file with more than one link, a `work/` that is a link, and anything outside a `work/` directory. A file over 1 MiB is shown cut, and a file that is not UTF-8 text by size and type only. The listing stops at 500 files, 2000 directories or 20000 entries, and does not enter a directory deeper than 6 levels; the page says what it cut.

**The runner's records are short.** The projected events drop Loom's `blob_digest`, so the page reads Loom's run log of the case, and the runner records no start, end or duration per action (`ui/README.md`).

**The old driver's records keep its names.** Records of past runs (`cases/**/evidence`, `experiments/`, the recorded run of `ui/test/recorded/`) keep the producer id `sdc-drive`, and the record `parity-loom-strong-4` names files that are deleted now.

**The cycles are not all converted.** Of the 131 names, 40 are converted, 15 are pending, 39 are held by Rust tests and 37 are dropped. The whole file is a slow lane, `task test:cycles-loom`; it was not run on this tree for this note, and `docs/cycles-suite.md` says that cycles run at a one-minute load of 100 to 177 ended on Loom's 60 s bound.

**`sdc-experiment` does not carry an effort.** It refuses `efforts.*` in a `loom` variant: the record format does not carry an effort to the runner yet, so the class defaults apply to a run it starts. `sdc-node --effort` and the settings file of `runbook run` do carry one.

**The daemon runs a stub unless asked.** `runbook serve` runs the stub runtime, in which nothing is executed, unless `--runtime loom` is given (`runbook/src/serve.rs`, `docs/engine.md`); the daemon's default confinement floor is `linux` and `local` must be asked for by name (`docs/daemon-api.md`).

**`--confinement local` is unconfined.** `local` is "unconfined and declared insecure" (`docs/loom-run.md`): a bound program can write the whole run directory. Under `--confinement substrate` the run directory is out of a bound program's reach (`docs/loom-run-decisions.md`).
**The child binary of `runbook run --loom` is still the one of `70b0e6e0`.** The library links `c9b4c177`; the slow lane `task test:loom-in-process` compares it with that child (`docs/loom-run.md`).
The rule approver (`SDC_RULE_APPROVALS`), the rework cap of the old driver and the end by rule `withhold` are not in the runner (`docs/loom-run-decisions.md`).

`task check:ess-suite:slow`, the byte comparison of a new synthesis with the committed suite, and `task docs:test` were not run for this release; the fast digest check is part of `task check:ess-generated`.

limits: The replay options of `runbook run` are refused. `--recorded` exits 64 with `--recorded is not built yet`; `--on-divergence`, `--live-adapter`, `--live-cap`, `--inject`, `--set`, `--take-recorded` and `--source-tree` exit 64 with `<option> needs --recorded <source>` without it.

No measured run of an evaluation has used this tree, and the release claims no measured change. The last records of runs through Loom (`experiments/parity-loom-strong-3.yaml`) were made with `runbook loom-run` on an earlier tree and decide nothing; no parity verdict between the driver and Loom exists.

The effort per node class of a settings file (`efforts.<class>.effort`, `SDC_LLM_EFFORT_<CLASS>` of the old driver) has no way into `sdc-node`, which takes the class default of `bindings/tools/node-classes.json`; this holds for `--dry` as well (`docs/cycles-suite.md`, row `efforts`).

The rule approver (`SDC_RULE_APPROVALS`, claims of the position), the rework cap of the old driver and the end by rule `withhold` are not in the runner: Loom's output holds no claim values and Loom has no such steps (`docs/loom-run-decisions.md`).

Six tests are ignored because the runner differs from the old driver (`git grep -n '#\[ignore' -- runbook/tests/loom_run/decisions.rs runbook/src/loom_run/decider/tests.rs`): `approved_on_checks` after three invalid replies, a rejection that names its case with exit 6, the decider's answer to a release at A3, a close at A5 taken by rule, a close at A3 asked of the decider, and a stop reason with no person.

Of the 130 cycle entries 36 are converted to the tree suite and 18 are pending (5 wait for a Loom story, 13 run and still fail); 76 are not converted. The whole file is a slow lane; neither it nor `scripts/run-finding-cycles.sh` was run on this tree for this note.

The daemon (`runbook serve`) runs the stub runtime unless `--runtime loom` is given; `stub` is the default (`runbook/src/serve.rs`, `docs/engine.md`). The Loom runtime is run through the slow lane `task test:engine-real`, not by the gate.
The old driver (`sdc-drive`, `scripts/run-trial.sh`) is still in the tree; `sdc-experiment run` no longer starts it, and no check of this note ran it.

releases.summary: A patch release after 0.1.0, the same day: the reject and cap routes of the audit, ways to keep a trial run going and to reopen it, a static route check and a pinned `canon simulate` step, workflow metrics with experiment records and a progress ledger, and the live view's run picker. No protocol of the nine changed. A source release at tag `0.1.1`; nothing is published to crates.io and no interface is stable. `CHANGELOG.md` lists the changes with their commits.

limits: Earlier runs' decisions were taken with the host's settings: until `f747085` the decider's model call loaded the host user's Claude Code setup (the `init` event of `runs/trial-3-strong-2/decider/001-q1/events.jsonl` lists 14 tools, 11 plugins, 60 skills and the host's output style) and took its effort level from the host's settings, which the runs do not record. The decisions of all seven passes are not reproducible on another machine as recorded. The hermetic adapter and an explicit default effort per class are in this release; no pass ran on them.

Before `50d90b9` the first real code review stopped every run: three runs from `main` at `8db4b93` with the real review node (`trial-3-strong-3`, `trial-3-strong-4`, `trial-3-mixed-7`) stopped `stuck` at their first `change.review` call with the reply file `out/review.json` unreadable. Fixed in this release (`50d90b9`); the runs through the fixed review node that passed are `trial-3-strong-6` and `trial-3-strong-5` above, whose tree is `main` plus that one fix branch, not this release's tree: the released tree adds the hermetic adapter, the effort per class, the re-raise fix, the bug-fix protocol and the audit, and its decider was not hermetic.

Five of the seven passes ran on `trial/3b` at `acd6f12` (`main` at `32265be` plus fixes that are all on `main` since), with the review step still a stub: no review model call ran in them. The other two ran on `trial/main-2`.

Three batch passes (`strong-1`, `strong-2`, `opus-1`) had no merge rejection. Rejections of `merge.approve` with rework occurred in two (`mixed-6`, `haiku-7`) and reviewed rejections in `strong-6` (2) and `strong-5` (4). The release reject route did not occur in a pass: it ends `not_delivered`.
Nobody started the delivered product; `haiku-6` and `mixed-5` show that a story set can pass every merge and still miss the idea (`docs/trial-3.md`).

Known faults, not fixed in this release: the decider's principal is named `decider:haiku` whatever model decides (`driver/examples/sdc/tools/decider.sh:5`, kind `haiku`; run record `trial-3-strong-1`: kind `haiku`, model Opus); the driver's "LLM calls so far" counts every started action of a binding with `llm`, including runs that called no model (`driver/src/main.rs:1033-1043`, printed by `scripts/run-trial.sh:291,712`; `docs/trial-2.md:519`: 18 calls in `llm-calls.jsonl`, 19 counted).
The bug-fix runs ran on `impl/bugfix-cycle` and not on this release's tree: the red-check defect fixed in `99238c0` is still in this release, and no scripted cycle covers `sdc-bugfix`.
The driver's runtime parts are a temporary copy of what the Loom runtime must provide (`AGENTS.md`, `docs/layers.md:51`, `docs/driver.md:43-45`).
Release and operate are being split out of the cycle (branch `proto/cycle-ends-delivered`); that is not in this release.
releases.summary: The first release of the SDC prototype: eight Canon `protocol/1` protocols for the cycle from an idea to a built, tested product, a ninth for one bug fix, the driver that runs them, and a live view of a run. A source release at tag `0.1.0`; nothing is published to crates.io (`publish = false` in the three crates) and no interface is stable. Paths are relative to the repository; a figure marked "run record" comes from `runs/`, which is not in git, and is stated as recorded there (`docs/trial-3.md` is the account of trial 3).
